- CSF analysis (if neurosyphilis suspected, though ocular syphilis may occur without CSF abnormalities)  
- OCT to assess for inner retinal ischemia or macular involvement (supports vasculitic mechanism but not specific)  
- Fluorescein angiography to confirm vascular leakage, capillary dropout, or periphlebitis pattern (characteristic of syphilitic vasculitis)  
- Vitreous tap or PCR (if infectious workup inconclusive — though syphilis is serologically diagnosed, not via aqueous/vitreous PCR routinely)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Syphilitic retinal vasculitis
